newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end lower, Chidambaram disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end lower, Chidambaram disappoints.

text.p: Indian shares ended lower on Monday as incentives offered by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on the weekend failed to enthuse the market, brokers said.
"The incentives aren't of much importance to investors," one trader said. "So the market is unlikely to run away."

Announcing incentives for investors on Friday, the finance minister doubled the limit on advances against shares to 1.0 million rupees, allowed foreign investors to launch dedicated debt funds and exempted investments in mutual funds from capital gains taxes.
In its latest strategy report, Lehman Brothers said it is overweight on the Indian market from a 12-month perspective.

"The situation currently is that liquidity is ample and relative yields are moving in favour of equities from a domestic investor perspective and with a forecast decline in interest rates and a pick up in economy later this year," it said.
The investment bank forecast a 12-month target of 4,750 points for the Bombay 30-share index, saying "the outlook for equities is positive."
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index lost 39.78 points or 1.13 percent to close at 3,468.29, off the day's high of 3,508.07.
The net traded value at the National Stock Exchange was 6.85 billion rupees in 37 million shares.
The Calcutta index dropped 4.16 points to 445.66 on dull volumes as lack of buying interest dragged prices lower.
"There seems to be a crisis of confidence among all large investors, " said Aprajit Sharma of brokers Jet Age Securities.
Delhi shares closed lower with the benchmark index closing 13.36 points lower at 776.01 points.
